title: Christie Snap Bean (Christie bean): Characteristics
metaDescription: Christie snap bean is a pole snap bean variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Christie snap bean is a pole snap bean variety, also sold or known as Christie bean or Christie pole bean. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Christie snap bean is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Christie bean or Christie pole bean, this is the same snap bean. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [snap bean variety finder](/crop-varieties/snap-bean), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 40 to 45 days after sowing. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit snap bean fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 40 to 45 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Pods: semi round green pods of 15 to 17 cm with black seeds, about 50 pods a plant.
**Where:** Suits warm areas such as Lucban in Quezon, and Laguna.
Early, with a long productive life.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual snap bean on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Christie snap bean

Baguio beans like cool weather, so most come from the highlands of Benguet and Mountain Province. Pole types bear longer, and bush types fit a short cropping gap. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

These are the closest matches among the snap bean varieties we list. So if seed of this one is hard to find, compare these first.

items.q: Is Christie bean the same as Christie?
items.a: Yes. Christie bean is another name for Christie. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Christie?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
